source_locator.quote: Video editing and synthesis often introduce object inconsistencies, such as frame flicker and identity drift that degrade perceptual quality.

claims.text: Video editing and synthesis can introduce frame flicker and identity drift that degrade perceptual quality.

source_locator.quote: To address these issues, we introduce ObjectAlign, a novel framework that seamlessly blends perceptual metrics with symbolic reasoning to detect, verify, and correct object-level and temporal inconsistencies in edited video sequences.

claims.text: ObjectAlign combines perceptual metrics and symbolic reasoning to detect, verify, and correct object-level and temporal inconsistencies in edited video.

source_locator.quote:
ObjectAlign consists of three stages executed in a closed
verification–repair loop (Fig.  1 ):

claims.text: The system runs metric scoring, neuro-symbolic verification, and adaptive repair in a closed verification-repair loop.

source_locator.quote: We treat each dimension of the feature vector 𝐬 i \mathbf{s}_{i} independently and learn a threshold vector 𝝉 = [ τ cos , τ hist , τ iou , τ lpips ] ⊤ \boldsymbol{\tau}=\bigl[\tau_{\cos},\tau_{\text{hist}},\tau_{\text{iou}},\tau_{\text{lpips}}\bigr]^{\!\top} from a small positive set 𝒫 \mathcal{P} (adjacent frames from the unedited video) and a negative set 𝒩 \mathcal{N} (pairs of original vs. edited frames, considered inconsistent).

claims.text: Independent thresholds for four consistency features are learned from positive adjacent unedited-frame pairs and negative original-versus-edited pairs.

source_locator.quote: A video is considered formally verified only if it satisfies both the low-level stability constraints ( 𝒞 neuro \mathcal{C}_{\text{neuro}} ) and the high-level temporal requirements.

claims.text: Formal verification requires both low-level stability constraints and high-level temporal requirements to hold.

source_locator.quote: Given a contiguous sequence of frames marked as inconsistent, we apply adaptive neural network based interpolation using RIFE  [ 19 ] .

claims.text: Contiguous inconsistent frame sequences are repaired using adaptive neural interpolation with RIFE.

source_locator.quote: Our experiments utilize a dataset of 95 text-to-video prompt pairs obtained from the DAVIS  [ 45 ] and Pexels  [ 1 ] datasets.

claims.text: The evaluation uses 95 text-to-video prompt pairs from the DAVIS and Pexels datasets.

source_locator.quote: Our primary baselines for comparison are PnP [ 53 ] , SDEdit [ 42 ] , StreamV2V [ 33 ] , and StreamDiffusion [ 27 ] without our object consistency corrections.

claims.text: The main comparison baselines are PnP, SDEdit, StreamV2V, and StreamDiffusion without ObjectAlign corrections.

source_locator.quote: All experiments were performed on one Nvidia 3090 GPU.

claims.text: All reported experiments were run on one Nvidia 3090 GPU.

source_locator.quote: For SDEdit, the score increases from 97.0 97.0 to 98.1 98.1 ; for StreamV2V  [ 33 ] , it improves from 97.3 97.3 to 97.9 97.9 ; and for StreamDiffusion  [ 27 ] , the score is enhanced from an original 95.5 95.5 to 96.2 96.2 .

claims.text: ObjectAlign increased overall-average CLIP score from 97.0 to 98.1 for SDEdit, 97.3 to 97.9 for StreamV2V, and 95.5 to 96.2 for StreamDiffusion.

source_locator.quote: Similarly, for SDEdit, the error is reduced from 105.4 105.4 to 100.7 100.7 ; for StreamV2V, from 100.0 100.0 to 98.7 98.7 ; and for StreamDiffusion, from 108.0 108.0 to 103.4 103.4 .

claims.text: ObjectAlign reduced overall-average Warp Error from 105.4 to 100.7 for SDEdit, 100.0 to 98.7 for StreamV2V, and 108.0 to 103.4 for StreamDiffusion.

source_locator.quote: The runtime overhead introduced by ObjectAlign is minimal, requiring approximately 3 3 % additional computation time compared to baseline PnP [ 53 ] editing, and 4 4 % additional runtime compared to SDEdit [ 42 ] .

claims.text: ObjectAlign adds approximately 33% computation time over PnP editing and 44% runtime over SDEdit.

source_locator.quote: Specifically, ObjectAlign relies on the existence of sufficient “consistent” keyframes to interpolate between them and reconstruct corrupted frames.

claims.text: The repair stage depends on having enough consistent keyframes from which corrupted frames can be interpolated.

source_locator.quote: If the edited frames are uniformly poor, such as containing pervasive visual artifacts or severe semantic drift throughout the video, then ObjectAlign cannot effectively recover a consistent video sequence, as no valid anchor points exist for interpolation.

claims.text: If edited frames are uniformly poor, ObjectAlign cannot recover a consistent sequence because no valid interpolation anchors exist.

method: ObjectAlign uses a closed verification-repair loop combining learned perceptual thresholds, neuro-symbolic consistency checks, and adaptive RIFE interpolation between consistent anchor frames.
problem: Edited and synthesized videos can suffer frame flicker, identity drift, and other object-level or temporal inconsistencies that reduce perceptual quality.
warnings: The source reports evaluation on a single Nvidia 3090 GPU and does not report physical edge-device measurements.
The source text contains duplicated digits in several rendered percentages and metric values; numeric claims preserve the values as displayed by the frozen source.
